findings.title: Indemnification plus mandatory arbitration and class-action waiver
findings.quote: You release, indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Promotion Entities, and their respective parent, subsidiary, and affiliated companies
findings.explanation: As a solo consultant you agree to defend and indemnify the sponsor and a long list of related parties for a broad range of claims (including IP infringement), and separately you waive class actions and must resolve all disputes through binding AAA arbitration under New York law. The combination of an indemnity duty with forced individual arbitration shifts meaningful legal and cost risk onto you for a hackathon with modest prizes.
findings.question: Can the indemnification obligation be capped or limited to third-party IP claims, and is opting out of the arbitration clause possible?

findings.title: Mandatory public Apache 2.0 open-sourcing of your submission
findings.quote: The repository must be public and open source by including an Apache 2.0 open source license file.
findings.explanation: While the rules say submissions remain your IP, this clause forces you to publish all source code, assets, and instructions publicly under a permissive Apache 2.0 license as a condition of entry. That means anyone (including the sponsor and competitors) can freely reuse your work, so you cannot keep the project proprietary or reserve it for paid client engagements.
findings.question: Is a public Apache 2.0 repository truly required for all submissions, or can judging be done via a private repo with granted access so I retain the option to keep the code proprietary?

findings.title: Arbitration venue and damages waiver
findings.quote: exclusively by final and binding arbitration under the rules of the American Arbitration Association and held at the AAA regional office nearest the contestant
findings.explanation: Beyond the arbitration mandate, you waive all rights to punitive, incidental, and consequential damages and to attorneys' fees, limiting any recovery to your actual out-of-pocket entry costs. For a non-US or non-New York consultant this venue and remedy restriction is worse than typical and worth understanding before investing time.
findings.question: Are entrants outside the US bound to AAA arbitration and New York law, and is there any carve-out for small claims?

findings.title: Rules can change at any time, including your obligations
findings.quote: The terms and conditions of the Official Rules are subject to change at any time, including the rights or obligations of the Entrant, the Sponsor and Administrator.
findings.explanation: The sponsor can amend the rules (including your obligations) after you have invested build time, with amendments effective simply upon posting to the website. Combined with the right to cancel, suspend, or modify the whole Hackathon in their sole discretion, this means the deal you enter under may not be the deal at judging.
findings.question: Will entrants be individually notified of any rule changes, and can material changes after submissions open be treated as grounds for withdrawal without penalty?

findings.title: Prize substitution and no fixed payment for non-cash awards
findings.quote: Sponsor in its sole discretion has the right to make a prize substitution of equivalent or greater value.
findings.explanation: The cash prizes are real and stated in USD, which is good. Standard substitution language and a 60-day payment window after returning required forms apply. This is normal for this type of contest but worth noting the payment is conditioned on completing affidavits and tax forms.
findings.question: None needed; standard terms.

findings.title: Taxes, fees, and affidavit requirements on winners
findings.quote: Winners (and in the case of Team or Organization, all participating members) are responsible for reporting and paying all applicable taxes in their jurisdiction of residence
findings.explanation: Winners bear all taxes, wiring/exchange fees, and must return W-9 or W-8BEN and affidavit forms within ten business days. This is standard for cash-prize hackathons but reduces the net value of the prize.
findings.question: None needed; standard terms.

findings.title: Promotional use of name, likeness, and submission for three years
findings.quote: the right to promote the Submission and use the name, likeness, voice and image of all individuals contributing to a Submission, in any materials promoting or publicizing the Hackathon and its results, during the Hackathon Period and for three years thereafter
findings.explanation: The promotional license is time-limited to three years (better than perpetual) and is non-exclusive, though the separate Publicity section grants worldwide use of personal information without further payment. This is ordinary promotional boilerplate.
findings.question: None needed; standard terms.

findings.title: Judges may be unnamed and criteria left to discretion
findings.quote: Judges may be employees of the sponsor or third parties, may or may not be listed individually on the Hackathon Website, and may change before or during the Judging Period.
findings.explanation: Judges need not be named and evaluation is at their sole and absolute discretion, but the five equally weighted criteria and a two-stage process are clearly defined with tie-breaking rules, which is reasonably transparent for a hackathon.
findings.question: None needed; criteria are adequately defined.

findings.title: Standard age and OFAC-based geographic exclusions
findings.quote: Individuals who are residents of, or Organizations domiciled in, a country, state, province or territory where the laws of the United States or local law prohibits participating or receiving a prize in the Hackathon
findings.explanation: Eligibility requires being 18 or the age of majority and excludes sanctioned regions and conflicted parties. This is standard and consistent between the eligibility section and team representation clauses.
findings.question: None needed; standard terms.

findings.title: Entry constitutes consent to data collection for promotion
findings.quote: Entry in the Hackathon constitutes consent for the Sponsor and Devpost to collect and maintain an entrant’s personal information for the purpose of operating and publicizing the Hackathon.
findings.explanation: Data handling is tied to Devpost's published Privacy Policy and limited to operating and publicizing the Hackathon. This is routine data processing for a contest platform.
findings.question: None needed; standard terms.

findings.title: 4 section headings have no body text
findings.explanation: These headings have no body text before the next heading: Winner; Prize; Qty; Eligible Submissions. On a page saved from the web these are often leftover navigation labels; in an authored document they are sections with undefined terms.
findings.question: These sections have no content: Winner; Prize; Qty; Eligible Submissions. What are the actual terms for them?

findings.title: Multiple dates appear near deadline language
findings.explanation: More than one date appears near the words deadline, due, submit, or submission: Aug 10, 2026, July 6, 2026, August 10, 2026. They may be different milestones or a real conflict. Review them by hand.
findings.question: These dates all appear near deadline language: Aug 10, 2026, July 6, 2026, August 10, 2026. Which is the final submission deadline?
